title: Science still has expertise; what it’s lost is authority
title_zh: 科学仍具专业知识；失去的是权威
abstract: In the years since the pandemic and the political turmoil surrounding the American scientific establishment, much time has been spent discussing why science has lost influence on public policy in the United States. A time when scientific advice about vaccination, nutrition, and environmental regulation was more readily heeded seems a distant memory. Scientific expertise has been decoupled from a sense of authority and standing to dictate policy on matters ranging from public health to climate change. The explanations for this separation include the rise of technologies like the internet and artificial intelligence, mistakes made by scientists and scientific institutions, and weaponization of anti-science ideas by political actors. But what if there’s a larger historical trend that suggests the disconnect between expertise and authority was inevitable? A new idea in philosophy called the “unicontext” suggests that the advance of technology, along with basic human desires, has been leading to this point for the past century.
abstract_zh: 自疫情爆发及美国科学界政治动荡以来，学界花费大量时间讨论为何科学在美国公共政策中的影响力下降。过去科学在疫苗接种、营养和环境监管等领域的建议更易被采纳的时代，已成遥远记忆。科学专业知识已与权威感和决定公共卫生、气候变化等议题的地位脱钩。导致这一分离的原因包括互联网和人工智能等技术的崛起、科学家及其机构的失误，以及政治行为者对反科学思想的武器化。但若存在更宏观的历史趋势，暗示专业知识与权威之间的脱节是不可避免的呢？哲学中的“单一语境”（unicontext）新概念认为，技术进步与人类基本欲望的交织，已在过去一个世纪里引导我们走向此点。
